correctness.rationale: PASS: Minimizing the exact truncated affine loss plus quadratic regularizer and proximal term gives two continuous affine branches separated by the kink x=(1+x)/2, with threshold c=[α(2−λ)−1]/[α(2+λ)−1]. On the invariant interval [0,1], the branch-order differences factor with positive denominators under 0<λ<1/3 and α>4/(1−3λ). Substitution gives x₀=(α+3)/D, x₁=(α+3+2αλ)/D, x₂=(α+3+3αλ)/D, D=α+3+4αλ; the strict itinerary x₀<x₁<c<x₂<1 and the three map identities prove a primitive period-three orbit. The return multiplier is (1−α)/[4(1+αλ)], so the stated attracting condition follows. The continuous interval map satisfies the hypotheses of Li–Yorke’s period-three theorem. The exact-rational checker inspects 64 rational parameter pairs and 10,112 finite minimizations; it is corroborative only, not the universal proof.
